newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian constructors sign Abu Dhabi mosque deal.
newsitem.headline: Italian constructors sign Abu Dhabi mosque deal.

text.p: Italian construction joint venture Impregilo -Rizzani de Eccher said on Tuesday it has signed a 625 billion lire ($411 million) contract to build the third largest mosque in the world in Abu Dhabi.

"The contract for the turn-key construction of the Grand Mosque for His Highness Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan the Second, President of the United Arab Emirates and Ruler of Abu Dhabi, was signed on November 2 in Abu Dhabi," Impregilo said.

Impregilo executives said at a news conference here the mosque would have a total area of 84,000 square metres, four minarets 110 metres high and 138 domes, and construction would take three and a half years.

The mosque, which will hold a total of 20,000 people in covered areas and courtyards, will have prayer areas totalling 52,000 square metres, eight times the size of a football field. St Peter's Basilica in Rome has an area of 25,000 metres.
Chairman Franco Carraro said the construction would be the third largest mosque in the world after those in Mecca and Morocco.

"The contract is one of the most important contracts in the history of contemporary building and definitely the most important building ever awarded to an Italian company because of its contract value, technical complexity and the quality of the decorations," an Impregilo statement said.

"It will be entirely clad in white Carrara marble, with mosaics in glass and marble, gypsum, brass, stucco and gilden wood, all for the impressive total figure - including floors - of 289,500 square metres," it said, adding this was 44 times the size of a football field.
Milan-based Impregilo, which is 28 percent owned by Fiatimpresit, part of the Fiat group, will have a 67 percent stake in the joint venture while Rizzani de Eccher will have 33 percent.
Carraro said an early payment of 15 percent, or around $60 million, had already been made and added: "We expect a profit of two percent on the value of the order."
Impregilo shares climbed 8.57 percent to 1,165 lire on the Milan stock market on limited volume following the news.
